classification.difficultyReason: Calculate an intermediate angle or variable before applying the converse parallel-line test.

content.prompt: In each case, decide if AB is parallel to CD. Give a reason why or why not.

spec.description: Unmarked lines AB and CD crossed by PQ; right-side interior sectors are 110° and 70°. Intersections are unnamed.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied angle givens are visible.

answer.short: Yes, $AB\parallel CD$: co-interior angles sum to $180^\circ$.
answer.worked:
$$110^\circ+70^\circ=180^\circ$$
The co-interior angles sum to $180^\circ$, so $AB\parallel CD$.

spec.description: AB and CD descend rightwards. Transversal meets them at Q and R. P is above Q. The 67° sector is lower-right at Q; the 112° sector is lower-left at R.
spec.mathematics: Angle PRD=112° by vertically opposite angles; 67+112=179, not 180.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied angle givens are visible.

answer.worked:
$$\angle PRD=112^\circ$$
Vertically opposite angles are equal.
$$67^\circ+112^\circ=179^\circ$$
The co-interior angles do not sum to $180^\circ$, so $AB$ is not parallel to $CD$.

spec.description: AB and CD descend slightly rightwards. PQR crosses them at Q and R. Upper-left sector at Q is 75°; lower-left sector at R is 105°. No parallel marks.
spec.mathematics: Angle AQR=180°−75°=105°, equal to its corresponding angle at R.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied angle givens are visible.

answer.short: Yes. $\angle AQR=105^\circ$, so corresponding angles are equal.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\angle AQR&=180^\circ-75^\circ\\\angle AQR&=105^\circ\end{align*}$$
Angles on a straight line sum to $180^\circ$.
The corresponding angle at $R$ is also $105^\circ$, so $AB\parallel CD$.

spec.description: Unmarked AB and CD crossed by PQ. Upper crossing is unnamed, with upper-left 6x and lower-right 72°. Lower crossing Q has upper-right 9x.
spec.answerVisibility: Expressions 6x and 9x retain their source form without degree symbols.

answer.short: Yes. $x=12$, $\angle PQD=108^\circ$, and the co-interior angles sum to $180^\circ$.
answer.worked:
Vertically opposite angles are equal.
$$\begin{align*}6x&=72\\x&=12\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\angle PQD&=9\times12^\circ\\\angle PQD&=108^\circ\end{align*}$$
$$72^\circ+108^\circ=180^\circ$$
The co-interior angles sum to $180^\circ$, so $AB\parallel CD$.
